title: Script import locks Stage 4 before review and lands on Stage 5
summary: Streamline routing with a usable screenplay sets stage 1 locked, stages 2 and 3 skipped (or imported) and stage 4 locked from the imported script, then the commit lands on Stage 5 because all of stages 1-4 have transitions; the user never reviews Stage 4 as a draft first.
notes: Contradicts the product-knowledge idea that a finished script lands at Stage 4 for review (WD-IDEA-FLOW-074); the Stage 4 lock is written by the atomic commit before the user sees it.

title: Location continuity warnings require force at shot-list lock but the UI calls them advisory
summary: Unresolved, ambiguous and scene-mismatch location counts add a warning to the lock validation; the lock returns 409 unless force is set, and the Stage 7 dialog offers Lock Anyway, while the copy says these location issues are advisory.
notes: Refines WD-IMPL-INVALIDATE-0053: the title says location warnings never block, which holds only in the sense that they are overridable by one confirmation, not a hard block.

title: Skip supersedes a draft or outdated stage with empty content
summary: The Phase A skip route and the streamline_commit skip transition refuse only when the latest stage row is locked; when it is draft or outdated with real content, a new skipped version with content {} becomes the latest row.
notes: Earlier draft versions remain in stage_states history, so nothing is deleted, but the active view loses the draft; the product-knowledge rule that skip is only from not-started (WD-IDEA-FLOW-080) is not enforced. The REST skip route has no frontend caller (WD-IMPL-ROUTE-0030), so the reachable path is the Streamline commit.

title: Shot extraction folds off-screen prominence into the background list
summary: The prompt asks for foreground, background or off-screen per character, but mapCharactersToForegroundBackground stores both background and off-screen characters in charactersBackground, so off-screen status is not kept on the shot.
notes: Any unrecognized prominence value defaults to foreground (line 173-174 comment and code); test coverage for this mapping not checked.

title: Shot continuity_flags reach the frame prompt but no Stage 7 UI shows them
summary: Extraction maps the LLM continuity_flags onto each shot; the Stage 9 starting-frame prompt builder inserts them as Continuity notes for the model, but no component under src renders or edits continuity flags in the shot list.
notes: The user cannot see or edit the flags in Stage 7 (grep of src for continuityFlags and continuity_flags in .tsx files found no match); persistence of the shots column was not traced column by column.

title: Extraction prompt says exactly 8 seconds but code keeps any LLM duration from 1 to 30
summary: The system prompt requires every shot to be exactly 8 seconds unless justified, but validateShot only discards durations outside 1-30 and extraction stores the LLM duration or the default 8; no clamp or justification check exists.
notes: The 8-second rule is enforced only by the model's compliance; the shot-validation warnings for durations outside 4-12 seconds (shotValidationService.ts:127-139) apply at lock time.

title: Blocking reference roles are reserved in type unions and a label map only
summary: The reference-role unions include blocking_composition_reference, blocking_start_frame, blocking_end_frame and the source blocking_reference, and the Stage 9 preview maps them to labels, but no code path assigns any of these roles or sources.
notes: Matches the product-knowledge statement that blocking roles are reserved but not built (WD-IDEA-SHOT-105); the grep for the role strings found only type and label occurrences.

title: Stage 4 generation is gated on Stage 3 beat content, not on Stage 3 lock
summary: Stage 4 load reads the latest Stage 3 content and requires beats to be present to proceed; the Stage 3 locked status is not checked in this path, so a script can be generated from unlocked beats.
notes: The lock predecessor rule (WD-IMPL-INVALIDATE-0002) still applies when Stage 4 itself is locked; this fact is only about generation.

title: Starting-frame prompt is told to carry camera position only, with movement reserved for video
summary: The Stage 9 starting-frame prompt builder instructs the model to extract only the static camera position (shot type, angle, lens) and ignore movement, and the video prompt builder instructs it to carry movement, so one camera string feeds two prompts with a split.
notes: Adds the camera-split behaviour that the AI entries summarise without stating; the split is prompt-level instruction only, not validated after generation.
